name: Partition of Jointly Owned Property (Meḥitza)
notes: Laws governing construction of partitions in jointly owned courtyards, including materials, thickness, cost-sharing, and ownership of fallen walls (Bava Batra ch. 1)

name: Residency Requirements for City Membership
notes: Laws determining when a resident becomes obligated in communal expenses such as walls and gates; twelve-month rule vs. purchasing a home (Bava Batra 1:5)

name: Presumptive Ownership After Three Years (Chazkat Shalosh Shanim)
notes: The specific rule that three years of working and profiting from land establishes presumptive ownership; different rules for irrigated vs. non-irrigated fields (Bava Batra ch. 3)

name: Claim Required to Validate Possession (Taanah)
notes: Requirement that possessor of land must provide a valid claim explaining how he became owner for the chazakah to be effective (Bava Batra 3:3)

name: Distancing Requirements to Prevent Damage (Harchakat Nezikin)
notes: Specific minimum distances required between various objects/activities and a neighbor's property to prevent damage: pits, trees, threshing floors, tanneries, dovecotes, etc. (Bava Batra ch. 2)

name: Neighbor Damage Rights (Hizkei Shechenim)
notes: Rights and restrictions between neighbors regarding windows, openings, noise, smoke, odors, and other disturbances in shared courtyards and adjacent properties (Bava Batra ch. 2-3)

name: Presumptive Ownership of Houses and Fields
notes: Specific application of chazakah to different types of property including houses, pits, cisterns, bathhouses, slaves, irrigated and non-irrigated fields (Bava Batra ch. 3)

name: Right of Way and Access (Zechut Derekh)
notes: Laws of access paths, public thoroughfares, private paths, and right of way including seller's right to access retained property through buyer's land (Bava Batra 4:2, 6:6-7)

name: What is Included in Sale of a House
notes: Detailed rules about which components are included in the sale of a house, courtyard, field, ship, or city when sold without specification vs. with 'all that is in it' (Bava Batra ch. 4)

name: What is Included in Sale of a Field
notes: Rules about what is included when selling a field: stones, reeds, attached produce, watch stations, carob trees, cisterns, etc. (Bava Batra ch. 4)

name: Field Measurements and Discrepancies in Sales (Beit Kor)
notes: Rules governing land sales where the area is specified by measure; what happens when the actual area differs from stated area, including the quarter-kav per se'a tolerance (Bava Batra ch. 7)

name: Order of Inheritance and Firstborn's Double Portion
notes: Detailed order of precedence in inheritance including son before daughter, descendants, brothers, and the firstborn's double portion; daughters' maintenance from the estate (Bava Batra ch. 8)

name: Sons vs. Daughters in Inheritance
notes: Distinction between sons who inherit and daughters who receive maintenance (mezonot) from estate; daughters inherit only when there are no sons; daughters' maintenance vs. sons' inheritance (Bava Batra ch. 8-9)

name: Bequeathing Contrary to Torah Order of Inheritance
notes: Ability to transfer property contrary to Torah inheritance order through gifts rather than inheritance declarations; deathbed gifts vs. inheritance orders (Bava Batra 8:5)

name: Tied vs. Ordinary Legal Documents (Mekuyyam)
notes: Distinction between ordinary (pashut) and tied/folded (mekushshar) documents; number of witnesses required for each; placement of signatures (Bava Batra ch. 10)

name: Erased or Contradictory Amounts in Documents
hebrew: שטר עם סכומים סותרים או מחוקים
notes: Rules when a promissory note contains contradictory amounts or erased text; principle of following the lower amount and the bottom entry (Bava Batra 10:2)

name: Guarantor After Loan (Arev she'Achar Matan Maaseh)
notes: Distinction between a guarantor who committed before the loan was made vs. after; Ben Nannas's ruling that post-loan guarantors have no obligation since the lender did not rely on them (Bava Batra 10:8)

name: Loan by Promissory Note vs. Oral Loan — Lien on Sold Property
hebrew: מלוה בשטר ומלוה על פה וגביית משועבדים
notes: Distinction between promissory note loan (can collect from sold/liened property) vs. oral loan or handwritten note without witnesses (can collect only from unsold property) (Bava Batra 10:8)

name: Pre-Wedding Gifts (Sivlonot)
notes: Gifts sent by groom to bride's father's house after betrothal and their recoverability if the marriage is not completed; depends on whether groom ate a groom's feast (Bava Batra 9:5)

name: Act of Acquisition for Deathbed Gift
notes: Whether a deathbed gift requires a formal act of acquisition or whether verbal instruction suffices; dispute between Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yehoshua/Eliezer (Bava Batra 9:7)

name: Will / Testament (Dayetikei)
notes: Laws of a written will or testament, its validity, requirements for delivery, and distinction between a will found on the deceased vs. one properly transferred (Bava Batra 8:6, 9:6)

name: Inheritance When Both Die Simultaneously (Beit Collapsed)
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel when house collapses on father and son or husband and wife and order of death is unknown; rules for dividing disputed inheritance (Bava Batra ch. 9)

name: Minimum Size for Division of Property
notes: Minimum sizes required before court will divide jointly owned property: four by four cubits for courtyard, nine kav for field, half-kav for garden, etc. (Bava Batra 1:6)

name: Two People with Identical Names in One City
notes: Problem of two people sharing identical names in the same city for purposes of legal documents; how to distinguish them and what happens to promissory notes when one is paid (Bava Batra 10:7)

name: Catacomb (Kever) Construction Standards
notes: Detailed laws on dimensions of burial chambers, niches (kukhin), and courtyards when constructing an underground catacomb (Bava Batra 6:8)

name: Acquired Privilege for Communal Easements (Chazkat Mavoi)
notes: Rules about when one acquires a prescriptive easement for use of another's property including spouts, gutters, windows, ladders, projections — fixed vs. movable structures (Bava Batra 3:6)

name: Trees Sold for Felling — What Seller Retains
notes: When buying trees in another's field — two trees vs. three trees and whether land is acquired; rights to new growth from trunk vs. roots; what happens if trees die (Bava Batra 5:4)

name: Acquisition of Produce by Pulling (Meshichah)
notes: Specific rules about when pulling vs. measuring effects acquisition of produce; when renting a place effects acquisition; different rules for flax (Bava Batra 5:7)

name: Honest Measuring and Weighing Practices
notes: Practical obligations of sellers: cleaning measuring vessels, dripping three extra drops, tilting scales for buyer, following regional customs for heaping or leveling (Bava Batra ch. 5)

name: Standard Building Dimensions
notes: Standard dimensions for various building types: small house, large house, banquet hall, bridal home, cowshed, and their heights proportional to length and width (Bava Batra 6:4)

name: Projections into Public Domain
notes: Prohibition on extending balconies and projections into public domain; acquired privilege of existing projections; digging underneath public domain (Bava Batra 3:8)

name: Giving Away All One's Property
notes: Rules for a person on his deathbed who writes away all his property; whether gift stands if he recovers; requirement to reserve some land; healthy person giving away all property (Bava Batra 9:6)

name: Erased Promissory Note — Ratification
notes: Procedure for ratifying a promissory note that has been erased: producing witnesses who remember its contents and having court issue a new ratification document (Bava Batra 10:6)

name: Receipt for Partial Debt Payment
notes: Dispute between Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei about whether to exchange note for smaller one or issue a receipt for partial payment; danger of receipt being destroyed by mice (Bava Batra 10:6)

name: Scribe's Rules for Writing Documents
notes: Rules about when a scribe may write a document for one party without the other being present: get, receipt, promissory note, bill of sale, betrothal documents, sharecropping contracts (Bava Batra ch. 10)
